title: An entitlement that applies automatically is recorded as a primitive with no parameters at all
content:
A.6.1.1.8.2.3.2.2.1.1 does something unusual for a Parameters document: it declines to have parameters. "Every Prime Agent is entitled to the Upkeep Rebate Primitive for tokens of other Prime Agents that they hold. Because this right automatically applies, there are no parameters."

The pattern is worth naming because the Artifact uses parameter presence as a signal of discretion. Where an Agent has choices — fee terms, token supply, Accord counterparty — the Instance Configuration Document records them, and they become editable through Root Edit. Where a right attaches by virtue of Agent *type* rather than by agreement, the configuration is deliberately empty.

The consequence is that an empty parameter set is a protection, not an omission. Because there is nothing to configure, there is nothing for Launch Agent 7 Governance to amend and nothing for a counterparty to negotiate away. The rebate cannot be traded, waived, or tuned at the Agent level; changing it would require changing what a Prime Agent is, at the Atlas level.

This is the same authority-partitioning logic seen elsewhere in the Artifact: put the levers where the right decision-maker sits, and remove them entirely where no Agent-level decision should exist.
description: The Upkeep Rebate Instance Configuration explicitly has an empty parameter set because the right attaches by virtue of Agent type — nothing is configurable, so nothing is negotiable.
